causal_chain: A separate counter-support branch can learn which historical items imply substitution or avoidance for that same target.
Candidate-conditioned retrieval of a few supportive historical items exposes which parts of a user's past actually justify a target item.
Sharper local margins during pairwise training improve global full-sort ranking at NDCG@10.
Subtracting counter-support evidence from support evidence produces sharper pairwise margins on hard negatives than unconditional user-item affinity alone.
Users with mixed or broad histories are poorly summarized by a single static preference vector.
blind_projection.closest_parent: Explicitly learning a user-conditioned exclusion memory and subtractive gate alongside standard attraction embeddings will improve ranking quality because many hard negatives are not merely low-affinity items; they are items that align with patterns the user's history implicitly avoids.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any observed gain could come from higher parameter count or generic use of user history rather than from candidate-conditioned support/counter-support routing itself.
discriminative_predictions: Relative to a matched mechanism-off control, gains should be larger for users with longer or more entropy-diverse training histories than for users with very short concentrated histories.

Removing only the counter-support branch after training should hurt ranking most on hard negatives that are close to the user’s positive region, while removing only support routing should hurt recall on niche positives.
The learned sparse routing weights should concentrate on a small subset of historical items for each candidate rather than remaining diffuse across the full history.
expected_evidence: A statistically meaningful NDCG@10 improvement over the matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
Inspection of routing distributions showing sparse candidate-specific historical evidence selection and non-trivial use of both support and counter-support branches.
Per-user analysis showing stronger improvements on mixed-taste users than on single-cluster users.
blind_projection.falsifier: If the matched mechanism-off control matches or exceeds full-sort NDCG@10, or if learned routing remains effectively uniform so that candidate-specific sparse support/counter-support selection does not emerge, the hypothesis is falsified.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This is a high-change proposal because it replaces static single-vector user scoring with a custom interaction structure: candidate-conditioned sparse retrieval over train-history items plus an explicit subtractive counter-support path. The change requires new executable capabilities for history tensor construction, sparse top-k routing, and full-sort batched candidate-history interaction, rather than a parameter tweak or a small loss wrapper.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local GeneralRecommender that scores each user-item pair by retrieving sparse candidate-specific support items and sparse candidate-specific counter-support items from the user's training history, then combining anchor affinity with support-minus-counter-support evidence, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over static pairwise collaborative filters because it can reuse the right parts of a mixed history while actively suppressing misleading co-consumption evidence.
implementation_requirements: For each sampled pairwise instance, compute candidate-to-history similarities, select or approximate sparse top-k support and top-k counter-support weights, aggregate history evidence, and score with anchor plus support-minus-counter-support composition.
Implement a custom RecBole GeneralRecommender with train-only user history caches derived strictly from the frozen training interactions.
Implement full-sort prediction with batched matrix operations over candidate items and padded user histories without accessing validation or test interactions.
Maintain user and item anchor embeddings plus trainable support-query and counter-support-query transforms for candidate-conditioned history retrieval.
Provide ablation switches for support branch, counter-support branch, and sparse routing so the executable mechanism-off and branch-removal falsification checks are run within the same codebase.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a matched control with the same embedding dimensionality, optimizer, pairwise loss family, and train-history availability, but replace candidate-conditioned sparse support/counter-support routing by mean-pooled history aggregation and disable the subtractive branch; keep comparable parameter count by retaining inactive projection layers where possible.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce candidate-conditioned sparse evidence routing over each user's training history, with dual branches for positive support and negative counter-support, and score items by anchor affinity plus retrieved support evidence minus retrieved counter-support evidence.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is the same backbone trained under the same protocol, except candidate-conditioned top-k routing is replaced by uniform mean pooling over the user's training-history item embeddings and the counter-support subtraction term is fixed to zero. This preserves history exposure and most parameters while removing the proposed sparse support/counter-support mechanism.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add a dual-branch sparse history router to a GeneralRecommender: for each target item, retrieve top-k supportive and top-k counter-support historical items from the user’s train history and compare against an otherwise matched mean-pooled history control.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does candidate-conditioned sparse support/counter-support retrieval from a user's train history improve NDCG@10 beyond a matched history-aware control that only uses undifferentiated pooled history evidence?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: A minimal implementation with padded history tensors, approximate top-k selection, and batched full-sort scoring should fit the stated qualification budget on ML-1M because histories are moderate and the model can cap per-user routed evidence to a small fixed k.
